P705
Parkinsonism related to progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity
and myoclonus
G. Rodier, C. Boulay, M. Anheim, S. Courtois, C. Tranchant (Mulhouse,
France; Strasbourg, France)
Background: progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity and myoclonus
(PERM) is considered as the most severe form of the stiff-man syndrome
(SMS). We present a case of parkisonism related to PERM.
Case report: A 21-year-old woman was admitted wit h a 1 year history of
back pain with painful spasms on lower limbs. The neurological exami-
nation disclosed proximal lower limbs pyramidal syndrom and paresis of
left 6th cranial nerve. Brain and spine MRI were normal. CSF analysis
showed oligoclonal bands. Six months later, spasms gradually became very
intense and painful with continuous muscle rigidity on her lower limbs.
The neurological examination showed a parkinsonism with left akineto-
hypertonic syndrome. Electromyogram revealed continous motor unit ac-
tivity in lumbar paraspinal muscles. Glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD)
antibodies were positives in the blood :1/4000 (normal range /H110211/80). No
neoplasic tumor was found. There was no response to levodopa. She
received high-dose intravenous immune globulin (IVIg) and symptomatic
treatment with diazepam. Few month later,there was partial relief of the
abnormal painful movements and parkinsonism.
Discussion: PERM is a rare neurological disorder, characterised by
muscular rigidity, painful spasms, myoclonus, and evidence of brain stem
and spinal cord involvement. Our patient developped an unusual parkin-
sonism. Clinical features, appropriate neurophysiological abnormalities
and highly positive anti-GAD antibodies led to the diagnosis of PERM.
IVIg was effective and diazepam remained useful in managing the symp-
toms. SMS and PERM are possibly both manifestations of a spectrum of
encephalomyelopathies having autoimmunity against GABAergic neurons
in common. Main pathological ﬁndings in PERM are perivascular lym-
phocyte inﬁltration and neuronal loss with affecting principally brainstem
and cervical spinal cord. Our case suggest a possible involvement of the
nigro-striatal pathway.
Conclusions: SMS and PERM should be considered in patients with
parkinsonism associated to unexplained back pain, stiffness and/or muscle
spasms. Early recognition and therapeutic intervention can signiﬁcantly
improve quality of life.
